text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance and location of your skin lesions, and when did the wrist pain and fever begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice a red, expanding rash that looked like a bull's-eye on your body about a month ago? Also, have you been bitten by any ticks during your recent camping trip in Minnesota?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists, combined with monoarthritis and a recent camping trip in Minnesota, is highly suggestive of Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia, such as Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. I need to rule out other causes, so REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, and Rickettsial serology.
